chunks: Ali ibn Abd Allah al-Warraq and Ali ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan known as Ibn Maqbarah al-Qazwini said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah said: al-Haytham ibn Abu Masruq al-Nahdi narrated from al-Husayn ibn Ulwan, from Amr ibn Thabit, from Sa'd ibn Tarif, from al-Asbagh ibn Nabatah, who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) turned from a tilted wall to another wall, so it was said to him, 'O Commander of the Faithful! Are you fleeing from the destiny of Allah?' He replied, 'I am fleeing from the destiny of Allah to the Divine Decree of Allah, the Mighty and High.'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Qada and Qadr according to Imam Ali (AS)?
ai.summary: This incident, recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *al-Tawhid*, illustrates the Shia theological distinction between *al-Qada* (the general, inevitable divine decree) and *al-Qadr* (the specific measure or manifestation of that decree). Imam Ali’s action demonstrates that while the outcome is predetermined, human agency (*ikhtiar*) allows one to seek the most favorable specific circumstances within the broader scope of destiny, a concept central to understanding divine wisdom and practical piety.
